GRAPH STRUCTURED DATA MINING

New Graph Neural Network Architectures
Due to the complex structures and large scales, it is hard to make predictions directly, thus the existing approaches turn to compress the meticulous structures into only two nodes with one edge, which may bring in noise and suffer from data sparsity. We call this the early summarization issue and propose Heterogeneous INteract and aggreGatE (GraphHINGE) to capture and aggregate the interactive patterns between each pair of nodes through their structured neighborhoods. [KDD 2020] [TOIS 2021] [🏆 AWS Machine Learning Research Project Award]

In order to bridge between symbolic semantics and subgraph topology, we propose ANalogy subGraph Embedding Learning (GraphANGEL) to make prediction of each node pair based on the subgraphs containing the pair, as well as other (analogy) subgraphs with the same graph patterns. [ICLR 2022a]
Simple Enhancements on Graph Neural Networks for Predictions
Graph neural networks and label propagation represent two interrelated modeling strategies designed to exploit graph structure. We propose a Label Trick to accommodate the parallel use of features and labels, which uses a randomly-selected portion of the training labels as model inputs, concatenated with the original node features for making predictions on the remaining labels. [DLG-KDD 2021] [🏆 Best Paper Award] It is foundational to many of the top-ranking submissions on the Open Graph Benchmark leaderboard. We further theoretically show that under certain simplifying assumptions, the stochastic label trick can be reduced to an interpretable, deterministic training objective. [ICLR 2022b]

SEQUENCE STRUCTURED DATA MINING

New Sequential Neural Network Architectures
Implicit feedback (e.g., user clicks) is an important source of data for modern search engines but heavily biased. We propose Deep Recurrent Survival Ranking (DRSR) that incorporates survival analysis techniques with recurrent neural network to derive unbiased estimations of user feedbacks. [SIGIR 2020a]

As users' demands are not only conditioned by their profile but also by their recent browsing behaviors as well as periodical purchases made some time ago, we propose Search-based Time-Aware Recommendation (STARec) which captures the evolving demands of users over time through a unified search-based time-aware model. [WWW 2022a]

With the prevalence of live broadcast business nowadays, live broadcast recommendation, is widely used in many mobile e-commerce Apps. We propose TWo-side Interactive NetworkS (TWINS) to fully mine the interactive patterns of both static and dynamic information on user and anchor sides, which is the first work for live broadcast recommendation to our knowledge. [WWW 2022b]

As user's multiple behaviors follow the behavior path "observation→click→conversion", we propose Hierarchical rEcurrent Ranking On the Entire Space (HEROES) which incorporates the contextual information to estimate these behaviors in a multi-scale fashion. [CIKM 2022]

Notice that Probabilistic Ranking Principle (PRP) would neglect the contextual dependence among the candidate items, and make the whole pipeline non-differentiable due to the sort operation. We propose Set-To-Arrangement Ranking (STARank) to directly generate the permutations of the set of candidate items in the context of the user browsed items without the sort operation. [WWW 2023a]
Simple Enhancements on Recurrent Neural Networks for Predictions
Despite elaborate architecture design, we reveal that incorporation of user feedbacks (especially feedbacks on previous item) as ranking features can significant improve the recommendation performance. [WWW 2022a]

We propose a simple yet sufficient unbiased learning-to-rank paradigm named InfoRank that can simultaneously mitigate the effects of both position and popularity biases by summarizing the impacts of those biases into a single observation factor, therefore providing a unified treatment of the bias problem. [WWW 2023b]

APPLICATIONS OF STRUCTURED AND UNSTRUCTURED DATA MINING

Sequential Recommendation Algorithms on E-Commerce Platform
Our proposed algorithms STARec and TWINS have been successfully deployed at China Merchants Bank and Taobao Diantao Apps. [WWW 2022a] [🔌 Real-world Deployment] [WWW 2022b] [🔌 Real-world Deployment]
Learning and Planning Algorithms on Ride-Hailing Platform
In a general view, there are two major decision-making tasks for such ride-hailing platforms, namely order dispatching and fleet management. Most of the previous work deals with either order dispatching or fleet management without regarding the high correlation of these two tasks. We propose CoRide to jointly model order dispatching and fleet management with hierarchical reinforcement learning. This research is supported by DiDi Athena Joint Talent Program. [CIKM 2019a] [🏆 Gaia Young Scholar Outstanding Project Award]
